definition: Upward mobility means moving into better life circumstances, especially in ways tied to greater economic success and quality of life. In this source, it is described as an outcome that higher education can help support.

reasons: The packet does not define “upward mobility” as “moving into better life circumstances.” It only uses the term in the context of higher education being able to “achieve economic success, upward mobility, and improved quality of life,” without explaining what “upward mobility” specifically means.

The definition’s specific phrasing (“especially in ways tied to greater economic success and quality of life”) is not stated in those terms; the packet lists “economic success” and “improved quality of life” alongside “upward mobility” but does not explicitly link upward mobility to them as a defining mechanism.

The packet uses “upward mobility” only in the phrase “higher education is a critical public health tool to achieve economic success, upward mobility, and improved quality of life”; it does not define the term as “moving into better life circumstances.”

The source supports higher education as something that can help achieve upward mobility, but it does not support the broader explanatory generalization in the definition about what upward mobility means.
